headline_marked: Protesters bring [[guillotine]] to AI data center meeting, developer rep flees
headline: Protesters bring guillotine to AI data center meeting, developer rep flees
summary: A $5.1 billion AI data center project faced intense opposition, with protesters bringing a guillotine to a city council meeting and developer representatives leaving due to safety concerns.
details: A public meeting discussing Verrus's proposed $5.1 billion Oakline at Mill Creek data center was disrupted by protesters, who brought a guillotine to the venue.

Developer representatives were confronted by a group of protesters during a break in the six-hour-long meeting, leading them to state that 'it no longer felt safe to stay' and requiring police escort.
Following the intense public opposition, Salem announced a one-year moratorium on data center developments, though Verrus's project may proceed as its application was filed before the moratorium.
Despite the moratorium, Oregon's governor terminated a deal to sell a portion of the land intended for the data center, forcing Verrus to revise its plans.

Oregon law requires large data center consumers to fund grid upgrades, which has led to increased electricity costs for such facilities while potentially lowering residential rates, yet community opposition persists.
